supersession.method: A new decision document, not an edit. Every E2 artifact that records a finding is pinned by sha256 below and re-checked before this task does anything; if one has moved, E2-R1 stops. Editing a superseded finding to match a later decision is how a record stops being a record.

e2_original_findings.missing_license_finding: No LICENSE file existed and packaging metadata carried the placeholder "Unlicensed - student portfolio project", so owner_license_decision_ required was true and no licence was chosen on the owner's behalf.
e2_original_findings.post_observation_python_correction: The frozen ci_python 3.11 was found incompatible with the resolved set because numpy 2.5.2 declares Requires-Python >=3.12. The frozen value was preserved and a correction block recorded changed_after_observation true.
e2_original_findings.installed_distribution_resource_resoluti: Fifteen modules resolve repository resources through paths relative to the source tree, so a wheel installs and imports but cannot reach configs, docs or mapping tables. No refactor was performed.

supersession.pinned_artifact_note: docs/e2_reproducibility_guide.md and docs/e2_data_license_review.md are NOT pinned. They carry no readiness verdict and no finding; they are operating instructions and a licence position, and instructions that have become wrong are a hazard rather than a record. Both are revised here, each with an explicit note of what E2 said and what changed.

license.copyright_line: Copyright (c) 2026 Thai Supply Chain Shock EWS contributors
license.osi_classifier_reason: Under PEP 639 an SPDX license expression supersedes the deprecated "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License" classifier, and setuptools 77+ rejects a build that declares both. The classifier is therefore omitted deliberately, not forgotten.
does_not_cover: OIE documents, index workbooks and the target data derived from them
any other third-party dataset or publication
prohibited_claims: the MIT licence applies to World Bank data
the MIT licence applies to NESDC data
the MIT licence applies to OIE data
the MIT licence applies to EPPO data
public download access grants redistribution rights
author_metadata: Thai Supply Chain Shock EWS contributors

citation.reason: CITATION.cff requires a verified personal author. None is available, and a citation file naming a person who has not approved it would be worse than none. The packaging metadata uses a collective attribution rather than a fabricated individual.

python_contract.later_versions_note: Metadata permits 3.13 and later to install. Nothing here has been run on them, so nothing here claims they work. Permitted is not tested.
python_contract.historical_311_record_note: Text that reports what E2 expected, and that it was found incompatible, is a record and is allowed. Text that tells a reader 3.11 is supported is a claim and is not.

supported_install_sequence: install the locked runtime and development dependencies
install the project from the repository in editable mode without independently resolving dependencies
prohibited_claims: installing the wheel outside the repository produces a functional runtime
the package can be installed from PyPI

packaging_limitation.statement: Fifteen modules resolve repository resources through paths relative to the source tree. A wheel installs and imports, but repository-level configs, docs and mapping tables are unavailable in an isolated installed distribution. No refactor was performed and none is authorised here. The limitation sits outside the chosen source-checkout scope, and it is the reason PyPI publication is not supported.

language_guards.pinned_documents_exempt_reason: The E2 record is guarded by checksum, not by language. It is supposed to say the candidate was blocked on a licence and that 3.11 was expected, because that is what was true when it was written.

high_entropy_classification.rule: a hex digest of 12 to 64 characters whose own line, adjacent line or enclosing mapping key names it as a checksum, digest, hash or fingerprint is a published content checksum; anything else remains a finding

reviewed_and_not_credentials.review: The scanner matched the secret-scanner setting in the pinned E2 contract, whose value is the scanner's own name. A configuration line naming the tool that enforces it is not a credential.
The same setting, repeated in this contract for the same reason.
An EPPO media identifier from the publisher's public REST index, recorded so a download can be traced back to the record that produced it. A public document id, not a secret.

metadata.name: thai-supply-chain-ews
metadata.author: Thai Supply Chain Shock EWS contributors

documented_nonblocking_limitations.statement: No CITATION.cff exists. It requires a verified personal author and none is available; the packaging metadata uses a collective attribution rather than a fabricated individual.
documented_nonblocking_limitations.why_not_blocking: A source-checkout release does not require citation metadata, and a citation file naming a person who has not approved it would be worse than none.

documented_nonblocking_limitations.statement: Fifteen modules resolve repository resources through paths relative to the source tree, so the built wheel installs and imports but cannot reach configs, docs or mapping tables. The wheel and sdist are built for content inspection only.
documented_nonblocking_limitations.why_not_blocking: The owner chose a source-checkout release, which is exactly the mode that works and the mode CI and the clean-tree verification both use. The limitation is blocking for a PyPI release and that is why PyPI publication is neither supported nor authorised here.

documented_nonblocking_limitations.statement: The supported floor is 3.12 and 3.12 is the only tested version. Python 3.11 is not supported: the resolved set requires 3.12 and above. Metadata permits 3.13 and later; nothing here has run on them.
documented_nonblocking_limitations.why_not_blocking: It is the owner's decision, applied consistently across metadata, both locks, CI and the setup instructions, and verified by reading all five.

documented_nonblocking_limitations.statement: 109 registered data-backed tests re-audit official third-party downloads. They are skipped by name and with a reason when those inputs are absent, and never counted as passing.
documented_nonblocking_limitations.why_not_blocking: The files are obtainable from their publishers and the acquisition code, URLs and checksums all ship. Tier 2 of the reproducibility guide is the route.

documented_nonblocking_limitations.statement: OIE, NESDC and EPPO state no terms of use; the archived World Bank Pink Sheet pages state none inline. All four remain unresolved and no raw byte from any of them is in the release.
documented_nonblocking_limitations.why_not_blocking: The conservative route is already taken: the bytes are excluded and only the acquisition code, URLs and checksums are published. Public download access is not a redistribution right, and the release does not behave as though it were.

documented_nonblocking_limitations.statement: Both locks were regenerated and verified on CPython 3.12 / Windows AMD64. They pin versions, not platform wheels, and have not been installed here on Linux.
documented_nonblocking_limitations.why_not_blocking: Every pinned version publishes cross-platform wheels and CI installs from these exact files, so the first CI run verifies the other platform rather than a claim made here.

documented_nonblocking_limitations.statement: 26 of 27 pinned distributions were covered by the vulnerability audit. ['packaging'] were not: pip-audit omits packages that are also dependencies of its own environment.
documented_nonblocking_limitations.why_not_blocking: No advisory was found for anything it did check, and nothing was hidden -- the uncovered pins are named. Reporting the package count without the gap would be the failure; a clean audit of most of a set is not a clean audit of the set.
